<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916754_theRebbe_640" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916754_theRebbe_640__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The maamar continues with the analogy of a physical war where all treasures are expended to achieve victory, explaining that this is because the root of victory is in the essence of the soul, beyond calculation, and likewise above, the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser, so to enable G-d's hosts to win, the treasure beyond revelation is given to them in a manner of wastefulness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the maamar continues,</t>
    <t s="1">that just as in a physical war,</t>
    <t s="2">in order to win the war, all treasures are expended,</t>
    <t s="3">for although in the ordinary way, not only are they not used</t>
    <t s="4">(even for a great need),</t>
    <t s="5">but furthermore, they are hidden and sealed from the eye of every beholder,</t>
    <t s="6">nevertheless, in order to overcome the opponent, all treasures are expended,</t>
    <t s="7">meaning not only are the treasures used, but they are even wasted,</t>
    <t s="8">for wastefulness is beyond measure, calculation, and limitation,</t>
    <t s="9">and the reason for this is that victory is rooted in the essence of the soul there,</t>
    <t s="10">(in the essence of the soul)</t>
    <t s="11">no calculations apply,</t>
    <t s="12">so too is it above,</t>
    <t s="13">that the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="14">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="15">in order for the hosts of Havayah to win the war,</t>
    <t s="16">they are given,</t>
    <t s="17">and in a manner of wastefulness,</t>
    <t s="18">the aspect of the treasure that is above</t>
    <t s="19">(above light and revelation),</t>
    <t s="20">about which it is said, "No eye has seen,"</t>
    <t s="21">in order to win the war and make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The explanation in the maamar that the reason for this is that the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser primarily refers to the giving of the treasure in a manner of wastefulness, because the intent of a dwelling place in the lower realms is in His very Essence, which is above reason, and therefore the power to fulfill this intent comes from His Essence, the treasure above light and revelation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this which is explained in the maamar, that the reason for this is that the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="2">is primarily regarding this, that the giving of the treasure is in a manner of wastefulness.</t>
    <t s="3">For this, that they give the treasure in order to make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="4">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that this is because the intent of a dwelling place in the lower realms is in His very Essence,</t>
    <t s="6">as the Alter Rebbe said,</t>
    <t s="7">in the precise language of our sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="8">"He desired... a dwelling place in the lower realms,"</t>
    <t s="9">for the matter of "desire" is above reason,</t>
    <t s="10">therefore,</t>
    <t s="11">the giving of power to complete this intent is from His very Essence,</t>
    <t s="12">the aspect of the treasure that is above light and revelation.</t>
    <t s="13">And the reason that the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="14">is</t>
    <t s="15">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="16">regarding this, that the giving of the treasure is in a manner of wastefulness.</t>
    <t s="17">And it can be added,</t>
    <t s="18">that the giving of the treasure in a manner of wastefulness to the hosts of Havayah to win the war is not only from the side of Above</t>
    <t s="19">(because the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser),</t>
    <t s="20">but this also pertains to the hosts of Havayah themselves.</t>
    <t s="21">For since their service is in a manner of wastefulness</t>
    <t s="22">(beyond calculations),</t>
    <t s="23">the folly of holiness that is above intellect and reason,</t>
    <t s="24">therefore they are fitting and vessels that the treasure from above be drawn to them in a manner of wastefulness.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The maamar continues in chapter 18, explaining that the concept that the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser is understood from the verse "And also the Netzách of Yisrael will not lie nor relent, for He is not a man to relent," meaning that the kingship of Shaul came from the aspect of "man," where relenting applies, while the kingship of Dovid came from the aspect of "not man," where relenting and change do not apply.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">D)</t>
    <t s="1">And the maamar continues in chapter 18</t>
    <t s="2">(the chapter relevant to this year),</t>
    <t s="3">that the explanation of the matter</t>
    <t s="4">(that the root of victory is in the innerness of Kesser)</t>
    <t s="5">will be understood based on what is said,</t>
    <t s="6">"And also the Netzách of Yisrael will not lie nor relent, for He is not a man to relent."</t>
    <t s="7">For this, that the Netzách of Yisrael will not relent, is because the root of victory is in the aspect of "not man"</t>
    <t s="8">(the innerness of Kesser),</t>
    <t s="9">and in the aspect of "not man," consolation and regret do not apply.</t>
    <t s="10">And the matter is,</t>
    <t s="11">that this verse</t>
    <t s="12">("And also the Netzách of Yisrael... will not relent...")</t>
    <t s="13">is Shmuel's response to Shaul regarding his request that the kingship be returned to him,</t>
    <t s="14">for after the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the kingship to Dovid</t>
    <t s="15">("and gave it to your fellow who is better than you"),</t>
    <t s="16">it is not possible that He will retract and take the kingship from him,</t>
    <t s="17">for He is not a man to relent.</t>
    <t s="18">And the Alter Rebbe, in Torah Ohr, precisely notes,</t>
    <t s="19">behold, from this very fact that initially the kingship was given to Shaul,</t>
    <t s="20">and when he sinned it was taken from him,</t>
    <t s="21">it is proven</t>
    <t s="22">that also above, relenting applies,</t>
    <t s="23">as it is explicitly stated in the verse,</t>
    <t s="24">"I regret that I made Shaul king...,"</t>
    <t s="25">and what does it mean when it says</t>
    <t s="26">(regarding the kingship of Dovid)</t>
    <t s="27">"for He is not a man to relent"?</t>
    <t s="28">And the point of the explanation in this is,</t>
    <t s="29">that the intent of the verse "for He is not a man..." is not only that the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like a lower man, to distinguish,</t>
    <t s="30">but rather,</t>
    <t s="31">primarily,</t>
    <t s="32">that He is also not within the category of the form of the Supernal Man.</t>
    <t s="33">And this is that regarding the kingship of Shaul it is written,</t>
    <t s="34">"I regret that I made Shaul king...," and regarding the kingship of Dovid it is written, "for He is not a man to relent,"</t>
    <t s="35">for the kingship of Shaul was from the aspect of "man,"</t>
    <t s="36">for in this aspect, relenting applies,</t>
    <t s="37">but not so the kingship of Dovid, which is from the aspect of "not man,"</t>
    <t s="38">for in this aspect, relenting and change do not apply,</t>
    <t s="39">as explained in Torah Ohr.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
